title: Tidewell Shipping — Capacity & Contract Playthrough
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on adding EU and APAC capacity, aligning on latency SLOs, and negotiating a six-month bridge amendment ahead of annual contract renewal. Customer wants a small dedicated pilot in EU and burst capacity for Black Friday window; questions about VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integration, and audit log retention. Agreed to run a 48-hour benchmark, send revised pricing and SOC2 + architecture notes, and follow up with legal/timing for contract amendment.
topics: current usage and forecast (Q1 surge + Black Friday)
hosted vs dedicated options for EU region
private deployment (VPC) and key management (KMS/HSM) requirements
latency SLOs and fallback model policy
billing/commit structure and short-term bridge amendment
transcript: [00:00:05] Jordan (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — capacity ask, contract cadence, security items, runbook for the EU pilot.

[00:00:28] Sofia (Head of Platform): yeah thanks Jordan, we have a spike forecast for early feb and then the big black friday window in november. want to make sure we don't get throttled — currently hosted has been fine in us-west but eu latency is rough.
[00:00:54] Markus (VP Eng): to add, we care about 95th tail under 220ms for 1k rps, otherwise our UX drops off. cost is also a hard constraint, we can't 10x spend.

[00:01:18] Priya (SE): right — so we can look at two paths: a small dedicated pool in eu-west for predictable throughput, or augment hosted with regional routing + cache warming. dedicated buys you the SLA but at commit cost.
[00:01:44] Eric (SRE): curious about failover — if dedicated in eu goes down how does traffic fallback? do we have automated model variants or are we shunting to different region with higher latency?

[00:02:12] Priya (SE): good q — Redwood's routing policy can fall back to us-west hosted or a lower-cost quantized model variant automatically. there is a config for max additional latency on failover. we've seen customers tolerating fallbacks for non-critical paths.
[00:02:39] Leah (Security): my main checkboxes are SSO/SAML, SOC 2, KMS integration for key custody, and ensuring audit logs for token usage. any PCI/PII notes? we need separation for payment tokens.

[00:03:06] Liam (CSM): we have SOC2 and ISO-27001 docs, and for KMS we support customer-managed keys via the private control plane — HSM is doable on-prem but there are specs. we'll share the architecture diagram.
[00:03:33] Sofia: ok good. Can you also confirm data residency options — logs stored in-region for at least 90 days?

[00:03:52] Ava (Solutions Architect): default retention is 30 days for request-level logs, but enterprise packages can extend to 365 with retained audit exports. for in-region storage we'll need a dedicated eu control plane or private deployment. that ties to the contract.
[00:04:19] Markus: so cost math — we need to know dollars per token for hosted in eu, and committed price for dedicated GPUs. Diego (pricing) — you here?

[00:04:36] Diego (Pricing): yep. rough numbers today: hosted eu token cost comparable to us-west minus some egress; dedicated varies by instance class. i'll run a scenario for 2x, 5x, 10x traffic with burst windows and show blended unit economics.
[00:05:02] Jordan: perfect. downstream question — for the 6-month bridge amendment, are we able to do a low-commit dedicated pilot then convert to annual?

[00:05:22] Liam: yes we can structure a bridge: 3–6 month reserved pool with a conversion credit if you sign an annual for next FY. we usually include a provisioning lead time of 4–6 weeks for new geo nodes.
[00:05:46] Sofia: lead time is tight for feb spike — 6 weeks pushes provisioning into late march. any faster short-term option?

[00:06:01] Priya: short-term we can onramp hosted eu with warm caches and prefix caching to reduce cold-start latency. also offer limited burst capacity from our shared pools if needed. that's less guaranteed but quicker.
[00:06:25] Eric: warm cache sounds useful — how does prefix caching interact with our request patterns (mostly chat+completion flows)?
[00:06:42] Priya: for chat flows we keep KV cache for session history. prefix caching will pre-warm frequent prompts. we can map your top 500 prompts and pre-seed the cache in the 48-hour benchmark.
[00:07:05] Markus: benchmark — can you detail the plan and what we'll get?

[00:07:20] Jordan: plan: 48-hour load run from eu endpoints, real sample traffic you provide (+ synthetic spikes to simulate black friday). we'll report latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, and cache hit ratio. SEs will instrument tracing.
[00:07:45] Sofia: timeline?
[00:07:50] Priya: we can schedule the benchmark next week — need a dataset and traffic profile by monday. we'll need an open endpoint or a sanitized sample.
[00:08:10] Leah: needs signoff from security before any live data is used — we prefer sanitized samples or masked PII. also need a copy of the runbook for data handling.
[00:08:32] Ava: we'll provide a runbook and the sandbox config. sec team can review and we can run with masked payloads. that still gives meaningful latency/cost numbers.
[00:08:50] Markus: great. back to contract: if we do a 6-month bridge, what's the cancellation clause and conversion credit?

[00:09:05] Diego: typical bridge has a minimum commit and a conversion credit equal to unused commit applied to the annual if signed within 90 days of bridge end. cancellation is pro-rated with 30-day notice. we can craft language for legal.
[00:09:28] Sofia: ok, Legal will review. we'll need pricing in writing and an amendment draft.
[00:09:45] Jordan: we'll send a proposal with two options: hosted regional ramp + burst, or dedicated pilot + conversion credit. include explicit SLA numbers and provisioning lead times.
[00:10:05] Eric: one more on fallback — can we set a per-route routing policy? some of our APIs are latency-critical, others are best-effort.
[00:10:20] Priya: yes per-route routing, with tags for criticality. we can set hard SLOs for routes and let non-critical routes fall back to cheaper quantized models. that's in the console.
[00:10:42] Leah: KMS — we want to ensure tokens are encrypted with our CMK, and we need HSM-backed keys for certain flows. what's the exposure surface?

[00:11:00] Ava: private control plane supports customer-managed KMS, and we can integrate to your cloud KMS (GCP/Azure/AWS). for HSM on-prem we have an on-prem package but that requires air-gapped or VPN connectivity setup. we'll include the technical spec.
[00:11:28] Markus: any performance hit with CMK/HSM?
[00:11:35] Priya: negligible for token encryption; key negotiation is occasional — per-request crypto ops are cached. we will surface any micro-latency in the benchmark report.
[00:11:58] Sofia: competitor check — we've heard back from HyperscaleHub and EdgeServe with lower list pricing but less transparency on infra. any calls out?

[00:12:12] Jordan: we mentioned HyperscaleHub and MegaCloud AI in earlier notes; key differentiation is observability + predictable throughput. you'll get trace-level token and cost breakdowns in Redwood Console.
[00:12:36] Leah: and SOC2 evidence? we need AICPA attestation and a pen test report if possible.
[00:12:49] Liam: we can share SOC2 Type II, and recent pentest summary redacted. will add evidence links in email.
[00:13:05] Sofia: sweet. any sticky points we haven't covered?
[00:13:10] Markus: one: autoscaling policies for dedicated — can you do scheduled scaling for predictable windows?
[00:13:22] Priya: yes scheduled autoscaling plus burst overrides. you'll be able to configure a cushion for expected windows and a manual override button in console.
[00:13:38] Eric: operational runbook — who is on-call from Redwood during a bridge pilot?

[00:13:45] Liam: dedicated customers get 24/7 on-call with an SE rotation and a designated CSM; for hosted we have standard support hours with pagerable escalation on enterprise tiers. we'll include the escalation matrix.
[00:14:05] Sofia: ok — recap me one more time: actions and deadlines?

[00:14:11] Jordan: sure — (1) Tidewell to send traffic profile + sample (masked) by monday, (2) Redwood to schedule 48-hour benchmark next tuesday-wednesday, (3) Diego to send two pricing options and draft amendment by end of week, (4) Redwood to share SOC2/pentest links and KMS spec. does that sound right?
[00:14:45] Sofia: yep, we'll aim for monday. legal loop might introduce lag but we'll try.
[00:15:02] Markus: one follow-up — can we get a sample bill run showing cost for projected volumes?
[00:15:16] Diego: yes i'll include a bill-run spreadsheet and three scenarios.
[00:15:30] Leah: please call out any data egress charges for eu->us fallback. we need to model that.
[00:15:45] Ava: noted, will include egress modeling and cache hit sensitivity.
[00:16:02] Speaker 1: (murmur) —
[00:16:16] Jordan: quick note — we'll schedule a legal check-in if the amendment looks standard; otherwise loop in your procurement.
[00:16:34] Sofia: sounds good. any open technical risks?
[00:16:42] Priya: one risk is cold-start for long sequence lengths; we'll advise a quantized variant plus prefix caching to mitigate. also KV cache size tuning during the benchmark.
[00:17:05] Eric: thumbs-up. can Redwood instrument tracing into our existing observability (we use Grafana/Prometheus)?
[00:17:17] Ava: yes there are tracing hooks and we can emit prometheus metrics via our exporter; we'll share the exporter config.
[00:17:36] Sofia: excellent. Logistics — who'll own the benchmark run coordination?
[00:17:43] Jordan: Priya will lead the run technically, Liam will coordinate scheduling and take notes. Diego will supply pricing. Jordan will shepherd contract language.
[00:18:05] Priya: I'll open a shared doc with the test matrix and waveform templates. need sample API keys for synthetic load. we'll not use prod creds.
[00:18:26] Leah: sec will only provide masked records; we may ask for a dry-run in staging first.
[00:18:45] Markus: ok — timeline recap: monday sample, tues-wed benchmark, friday proposal? is that compressed?
[00:18:58] Diego: i'll try to draft by friday EOD. if legal iterations take longer we'll extend.
[00:19:14] Jordan: wrap-up — next meeting provisional for the week after benchmark to review results and agree on amendment. we'll send calendar invite. any last questions?
[00:19:29] Sofia: none from me. thanks everyone.
[00:19:34] Markus: thanks — bye.
[00:19:38] Jordan: bye.
